title: When the IBKR gateway is connected, use it exclusively for market data instead of yfinance/Stooq
description:
User-requested change (raised in conversation while diagnosing ticker-detail-view slowness caused by yfinance being rate-limited, docs/tasks/backend-data-provider-timeouts.json): whenever the IBKR Client Portal Gateway is connected/available, this app should source market data from IBKR exclusively -- daily/weekly OHLCV, and whatever else `DataProvider` currently supplies -- and not call yfinance/Stooq at all in that case, not even as a fallback on a per-call error. Only when IBKR isn't connected (disabled, gateway unreachable, not authenticated) should the app fall back to today's yfinance-primary/Stooq-fallback behavior.

This directly reverses an existing, explicit design decision recorded in `IBKRProvider`'s own module docstring: 'That makes it a poor fit as this app's *primary* data source (unlike `YFinanceProvider`'s always-on, no-login-step nature) -- it's used only for the specific extra capabilities it uniquely unlocks' (hourly bars for day-trader mode, the market scanner). `IBKRProvider` also deliberately does *not* implement the `DataProvider` protocol (`app/data/base.py`) today -- see that same docstring's rationale (its capabilities 'don't map onto that protocol's `get_daily_ohlcv`/`get_weekly_ohlcv`/`get_extended_data` shape at all'). Implementing this task means revisiting that decision with the new requirement in hand, not silently working around it -- record the reversal and why as a `decisions` entry per CLAUDE.md's decision-memory convention, referencing the original rationale being superseded.

Open research questions to resolve before/while implementing (don't assume -- confirm against a live gateway, the same way every other IBKR-provider fact in this codebase has been confirmed rather than guessed from docs, per `IBKRProvider`'s own 'Testing constraint' docstring paragraph and this session's own experience finding two live-gateway-only bugs in the scanner path):
- Can `/iserver/marketdata/history` (already wrapped by `IBKRProvider.get_hourly_bars`, whose `_VALID_BAR_INTERVALS`/`_BAR_INTERVAL_STEP` already include `'1d'`/`'1w'`) actually serve full-history daily/weekly bars for an arbitrary held/watched ticker the way `YFinanceProvider.get_daily_ohlcv`/`get_weekly_ohlcv` do today, or does it have a shorter lookback ceiling that makes it unsuitable for Screen 1's 26-week-minimum requirement or the various whole-history passes (support/resistance zones, Autoenvelope channel, insider-cluster detection) that assume deep history?
- `get_extended_data` (earnings/dividend dates, short interest, insider transactions) has no obvious IBKR Client Portal Web API equivalent researched yet anywhere in this codebase/docs/ideas.md -- confirm whether IBKR's API can supply any of these at all. If it can't, 'use IBKR for everything' may need a carve-out (e.g. extended data keeps using yfinance/Stooq even while IBKR is otherwise primary) -- decide and record rather than silently guessing either way.
- Every ticker needs an IBKR conid before any of its endpoints are usable (`IBKRProvider.resolve_conid`, one `/iserver/secdef/search` round trip per ticker) -- decide whether/how this gets cached (today nothing caches conid resolutions across requests) so switching to IBKR-primary doesn't add a resolution round trip to every single request for every ticker.
- How 'IBKR is connected' is checked per request without adding a slow, real network round trip (`get_gateway_status` hits `/iserver/auth/status` live) to every single market-data call -- reuse/extend the existing singleton (`app.api.dependencies._get_ibkr_provider_singleton`) and its existing caching patterns (e.g. `get_scanner_params`'s 15-minute TTL cache) rather than inventing a third caching scheme.
- The user's own instruction is explicit that no yfinance/Stooq fallback should happen while IBKR is connected, even on a single call's own failure (e.g. an unresolvable conid, a transient IBKR-side error) -- this removes the resilience a fallback would otherwise provide. Decide and record (as a `decisions` entry, not silently) what such a per-call failure should do instead: presumably the same graceful-degradation contract this app already uses elsewhere (a null/degraded field, or the existing `DataProviderUnavailableError` -> 503 path) rather than ever silently reaching for yfinance.

Applies to every caller of `get_data_provider` (`app.api.dependencies`), not just the ticker detail view that prompted this -- `GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/analysis`, `GET /api/watchlist` (+ breadth), `GET /api/portfolio` (+ risk), and `GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/indicator-history` all share this same dependency and would all switch together.

checklist.step: Research (against a live gateway, not just documented assumptions) whether /iserver/marketdata/history can serve the same daily/weekly history depth get_daily_ohlcv/get_weekly_ohlcv need, and whether any IBKR endpoint can supply an equivalent to get_extended_data's earnings/dividend/short-interest/insider-transaction fields. Record findings and any resulting scope carve-outs as a decisions entry.
Decide and record (decisions entry) how IBKR conid resolution is cached across requests so switching to IBKR-primary doesn't add a resolve_conid round trip per ticker per request.

Decide and record (decisions entry) how 'IBKR is connected' is determined per request cheaply (reusing/extending the existing singleton + caching patterns already in app.api.dependencies/IBKRProvider), and how a mid-request IBKR-specific failure degrades given the no-yfinance-fallback-while-connected constraint.

Record the reversal of IBKRProvider's existing 'not a primary data source, doesn't implement DataProvider' design decision as a decisions entry, referencing the original rationale (its own module docstring) being superseded and why.

Implement: either make IBKRProvider satisfy the DataProvider protocol or add a new adapter that does, and wire app.api.dependencies.get_data_provider to return it instead of CachedDataProvider(YFinanceProvider(), StooqProvider(), db) whenever IBKR is connected/available, falling back to today's yfinance/Stooq behavior only when it isn't.

Tests: provider-selection logic (IBKR-connected vs not) with mocked IBKR responses matching whatever live-gateway shapes were confirmed in the research step (mirroring tests/unit/data/test_ibkr_provider.py's existing mocked-HTTP-boundary convention -- no live network calls per docs/architecture/Testing.md), plus a regression assertion that yfinance/Stooq are never invoked while IBKR is connected.

decisions.decision: Checklist item 1 live-gateway research findings: (1) /iserver/marketdata/history's response is hard-capped at ~999-1000 bars per request regardless of bar size (matches docs/ideas.md's documented 'max 1,000 data points per call', already _MAX_BARS_PER_PAGE in ibkr_provider.py). For bar='1d' against AAPL's real conid (265598), period values from '4y' up through 'max'/'20y' all returned the identical 999-bar response starting 2022-10-06 -- i.e. IBKR's actual daily-bar retention ceiling for this gateway/entitlement is ~4 calendar years, NOT whatever larger period is requested. For bar='1w', period='5y' returned 261 bars, '10y' returned 522 bars, and '20y' returned the full 1000-bar cap reaching back to 2007-08-06 (~19 calendar years) -- weekly bars scale with the requested period up to the same 1000-bar ceiling. Both comfortably exceed docs/Analyse.md's own documented minimum ('daily OHLCV history (minimum ~200 trading days)') and Screen 1's 26-week-minimum (YFinanceProvider._MIN_WEEKLY_BARS=26) -- so IBKR-primary OHLCV is viable depth-wise even though it's materially shallower than yfinance's decades-deep 'full available history' for an older ticker (a real, accepted reduction in how far back support/resistance-zone/Autoenvelope history can reach, not something this task's modest documented minimums require fixing). (2) No IBKR Client Portal Web API endpoint supplies an equivalent to get_extended_data's earnings/dividend/short-interest/insider-transaction fields: tried /iserver/fundamentals/{conid}/summary (400 'Data not available'), /fundamentals/{conid}/summary (404, route doesn't exist on this gateway build), /iserver/fundamentals/{conid}/financial-statements|key-ratios|dividends (all 404), and /iserver/marketdata/snapshot with several documented dividend/earnings field codes (7287-7293, 7636) -- returned only conid/company-name fields, nothing financial (this account/gateway has no market-data-subscription entitlement for those snapshot fields). /iserver/secdef/info and /iserver/contract/{conid}/info both work (200, real contract metadata) but carry no earnings/dividend/short-interest/insider data at all.
decisions.rationale: Resolves this task's own flagged research questions rather than guessing either way. Depth: a single, unpaginated request per bar size already meets every documented minimum this app actually needs, so IBKR-primary OHLCV is implemented without deep-pagination (see the separate decision below on get_daily_bars/get_weekly_bars's own single-request design). Extended data: since IBKR genuinely has no equivalent and this is a Client Portal Web API / account-entitlement limitation (not a transient failure), extended data (earnings_date/ex_dividend_date/shares_short/short_ratio/short_percent_of_float/float_shares/insider_transactions) is carved out as a permanent, structural exception -- IBKRPrimaryDataProvider (app/data/ibkr_data_provider.py) delegates get_extended_data entirely to the existing cached yfinance/Stooq chain even while IBKR is primary for OHLCV, rather than ever attempting to serve it from IBKR or returning degraded nulls for a capability a human would reasonably still want working. This is explicitly not a 'yfinance fallback on a per-call failure' (which the task's own description rules out while IBKR is connected) -- it's a permanent routing decision for a category of data IBKR cannot ever serve on this integration, made once at composition time, not retried per call.

decisions.decision: IBKRProvider.get_daily_bars/get_weekly_bars (new methods, app/data/ibkr_provider.py) each issue a single /iserver/marketdata/history request (period='10y'/bar='1d' and period='20y'/bar='1w' respectively) rather than reusing get_hourly_bars's existing multi-page pagination loop.
decisions.rationale: Two reasons, both confirmed live during checklist item 1's research: (1) the chosen period values already sit at or past IBKR's own confirmed response ceiling for each bar size (see the research decision above), so a second page would have nothing further to return anyway. (2) get_hourly_bars's own pagination-stop heuristic ('a short page -- fewer than _MAX_BARS_PER_PAGE rows -- means there's nothing further back') was found live to be actually WRONG for bar='1d' specifically: requesting a second page by combining startTime with period (not startTime alone, which returned 0 bars every time it was tried) returned a further 999 OLDER daily bars (2018-10-17 to 2022-10-05) even though the first page's row count was already one short of the full 1,000-bar page size. Inheriting get_hourly_bars's loop here would have silently under-reported history by a full page in exactly the method this task needs to get right. A single, unpaginated request avoids reproducing that latent bug entirely. Deeper multi-page daily/weekly history (to more closely match yfinance's decades-deep 'full available history') is explicitly out of scope here given this task's own 'scope conservatively' guidance -- docs/Analyse.md's documented minimums are already comfortably covered by the single-page depth confirmed above -- and is left as a potential future enhancement, not filed as a tracked followup since nothing today needs it.

decisions.decision: Checklist item 2: IBKRProvider.resolve_conid caches its result (including a None/unresolved result) per uppercased ticker, in-memory on the IBKRProvider instance itself (a new self._conid_cache dict), with a 24-hour TTL (_CONID_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS) matching app.data.cache._CACHE_TTL's own OHLCV freshness window.
decisions.rationale: Reuses the exact in-instance TTL-cache pattern get_scanner_params already established on this same class (self._scanner_params_cache), per this task's own instruction not to invent a third caching scheme. Caching lives on IBKRProvider itself (not on the new ticker-keyed adapter) so every current and future caller of resolve_conid benefits, and so it's naturally shared via the existing process-wide singleton (app.api.dependencies._get_ibkr_provider_singleton) across every request, not re-created per request. 24h was chosen because a ticker's IBKR conid mapping only changes on a genuine listing event (new IPO conid, re-listing after a symbol change) -- never intraday -- so there's no freshness reason to cache it for less time than the OHLCV data it's resolved in service of. A None (ambiguous/unknown) result is cached on the same TTL rather than left unconditionally uncached: re-querying /iserver/secdef/search on every single call for a ticker IBKR has already definitively failed to resolve would defeat the point of caching for exactly the tickers most likely to be requested repeatedly. This surfaced a concrete, previously-untested real-world case during this task's own live-gateway research: searching for 'AAPL' itself returns FOUR distinct STK-sectioned conids (NASDAQ primary listing 265598, a TSE-CDR listing, a Mexico-exchange listing, and an EBS listing), which _resolve_stk_conid's existing (and out-of-scope-to-change-here) ambiguity rule -- more than one distinct conid for an exact symbol match degrades to None -- treats as unresolvable. This means AAPL itself, the most common example ticker in this codebase's own tests/docs, cannot be resolved via a bare symbol search against this live gateway today. Not fixed in this task (see the separate followups decision below) -- resolve_conid's ambiguity-degrades-to-None behavior is an existing, already-reviewed design decision from backend-ibkr-symbol-resolution, and adding exchange/listing disambiguation here would be a substantial scope expansion this task's own 'scope conservatively' guidance argues against; the caching behavior above still applies correctly to this (and every other) outcome regardless.

decisions.decision: Checklist item 3a (connectivity check): IBKRProvider.get_gateway_status itself now caches its result in-memory (self._gateway_status_cache) for _GATEWAY_STATUS_TTL_SECONDS = 5 seconds, shared by every caller including each data-fetching method's own internal _require_available() guard. Checklist item 3b (mid-request failure degradation): a per-call IBKR failure while connected raises DataProviderUnavailableError (-> HTTP 503 at the API layer, the app's existing graceful-degradation contract), achieved structurally by passing the same IBKRDataProvider instance as BOTH the primary and the fallback argument to CachedDataProvider in app.api.dependencies._build_ibkr_primary_data_provider, rather than ever passing a YFinanceProvider/StooqProvider as the fallback while IBKR is connected.
decisions.rationale: 3a: caching directly inside get_gateway_status (rather than only in a separate dependencies.py-level check) means app.api.dependencies' own per-request 'is IBKR connected' check AND every IBKRProvider method's pre-existing _require_available() guard share one cached result -- a caller that already checked connectivity via get_data_provider doesn't pay for a second live /iserver/auth/status round trip moments later when an actual data call runs. 5 seconds (vs. get_scanner_params's existing 15-minute TTL, which exists to respect an IBKR-documented per-endpoint rate limit rather than for latency) is a pure latency/freshness trade-off: there's no documented rate limit on /iserver/auth/status to respect, and this task's own live-gateway research observed the gateway's authenticated state flip within MINUTES (not seconds) across a resumed session, so a few seconds of staleness is a cost worth paying to collapse a request's own fan-out of several per-ticker calls (or a tight sequence of HTTP requests) into effectively one real status check. Accepted, documented side effect: GET /api/ibkr/status can now report a result up to 5 seconds stale (noted directly in that route's own docstring) rather than threading a 'bypass the cache' parameter through just for that one read-only endpoint. 3b: CachedDataProvider's existing 'try primary, on DataProviderUnavailableError try fallback' logic, given the identical instance for both roles, degrades to a pure retry of IBKR itself -- which will almost always fail the same way immediately after, surfacing a clean DataProviderUnavailableError (both attempts report the same underlying IBKR failure) without ever touching yfinance/Stooq, while still getting CachedDataProvider's SQLite OHLCV read-through cache for free. Considered and rejected: a bespoke 'no-op fallback' DataProvider class that immediately re-raises -- the self-as-fallback approach reuses an already-battle-tested code path (CachedDataProvider) with zero new logic, at the cost of a less obvious-at-a-glance primary==fallback wiring, which is why it's called out explicitly in _build_ibkr_primary_data_provider's own docstring rather than left to look like an accidental duplicate argument.

decisions.decision: Checklist item 4: IBKRProvider's own module docstring (app/data/ibkr_provider.py) has been updated to record that this task reverses its prior 'poor fit as a primary data source' design decision -- IBKR is now used as this app's primary market-data source (daily/weekly OHLCV) whenever its gateway is connected/authenticated, via a new ticker-keyed adapter (app.data.ibkr_data_provider.IBKRDataProvider) rather than by IBKRProvider itself implementing the DataProvider protocol directly.
decisions.rationale: The original decision's underlying structural reason (the gateway's interactive-login/session-keepalive requirements make it unlike YFinanceProvider's always-on nature) still holds and still fully motivates this app's fallback behavior for when no gateway is connected -- it just no longer rules IBKR out as primary WHEN a human already has their own gateway logged in, which is the literal, explicit user request this task implements. IBKRProvider itself still does not implement DataProvider directly (its methods remain conid-keyed, not ticker-keyed) -- that choice from the original decision stands unchanged; only the 'IBKR can never be primary' half of the original rationale is reversed, via a separate adapter layer rather than retrofitting IBKRProvider's own signatures.

decisions.decision: Checklist item 5 implementation shape: a new module app/data/ibkr_data_provider.py defines two classes -- IBKRDataProvider (a thin DataProvider-protocol adapter: ticker -> resolve_conid -> get_daily_bars/get_weekly_bars -> a pandas frame matching the protocol's column/index shape; get_extended_data always reports unavailable_reason='fallback_provider_active' and is never actually reached through the normal wiring) and IBKRPrimaryDataProvider (a pure router: OHLCV to one injected DataProvider, extended data to a separate injected DataProvider). app.api.dependencies gains _is_ibkr_connected() (Settings.ibkr_enabled AND the singleton's get_gateway_status().state == 'available'), _build_live_data_provider() (shared by both get_data_provider and get_data_provider_factory's _live_scope, so both pick the same source for the same gateway state), and _build_ibkr_primary_data_provider() (constructs CachedDataProvider(ibkr_adapter, ibkr_adapter, db) for OHLCV + CachedDataProvider(YFinanceProvider(), StooqProvider(), db) for extended data, wrapped in IBKRPrimaryDataProvider). An unresolvable ticker (resolve_conid returns None, whether genuinely unknown to IBKR or ambiguous across more than one listing) or a resolved conid with zero returned bars both raise TickerNotFoundError, matching the existing YFinanceProvider/StooqProvider convention of mapping 'this provider has no usable data for this ticker' to that same exception/404.
decisions.rationale: Two classes rather than one: IBKRDataProvider is pure ticker->conid->bars mechanics with zero composition/caching opinion, independently testable and reusable; IBKRPrimaryDataProvider is pure routing with zero IBKR-specific knowledge, so the composition app.api.dependencies builds is easy to reason about and test in isolation (see tests/unit/data/test_ibkr_data_provider.py). Deliberately does NOT build IBKRPrimaryDataProvider as a bare CachedDataProvider instance whose own inherited get_extended_data is relied upon: CachedDataProvider's own get_extended_data has its own SQLite caching layer, and chaining it through IBKRDataProvider down to a second, inner CachedDataProvider(YFinanceProvider(), StooqProvider(), db) would read/write the same ExtendedDataCacheORM row through two redundant caching layers -- IBKRPrimaryDataProvider instead routes get_extended_data directly to the single cached yfinance/Stooq chain, bypassing the OHLCV CachedDataProvider entirely for that one method. get_data_provider_factory's _live_scope (used by GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/analysis) was updated to share the exact same _build_live_data_provider helper as get_data_provider, even though this task's own description technically listed that route under 'callers of get_data_provider' (it actually calls the factory) -- left inconsistent, that route would have kept using yfinance/Stooq even while every other route switched to IBKR, which is exactly the kind of silent drift CLAUDE.md's decision-memory convention exists to avoid. TickerNotFoundError for an ambiguous resolution (not a distinct new exception/semantic): the DataProvider protocol's existing exception hierarchy (app/data/exceptions.py) has no 'ambiguous, exists but can't disambiguate automatically' case, and from this provider's own perspective 'ambiguous' and 'unknown' both mean the same practical thing -- no usable IBKR data for this ticker -- so reusing the existing 404 mapping is more honest than either inventing a new exception type for one provider or stretching DataProviderUnavailableError's 'the whole provider is down' semantics to cover a per-ticker outcome.

decisions.decision: Scope carve-outs deliberately left for a follow-up task rather than addressed here: (1) resolve_conid's existing ambiguity-degrades-to-None behavior means a cross-listed ticker like AAPL itself cannot be served by IBKR-primary mode via a bare symbol search -- adding exchange/listing-preference disambiguation to _resolve_stk_conid is out of scope for this task. (2) backend/openapi.json and frontend/src/api/types.ts were found to already be stale relative to each other BEFORE this task's own changes (regenerating both via scripts/export_openapi.py / yarn generate:api-types pulled in several unrelated, already-merged backend docstring updates that were apparently never followed by a frontend types regeneration) -- this task's own change (a docstring addition to GET /api/ibkr/status's description, no schema/route-signature change) was reverted out of both generated files rather than committed bundled with that unrelated pre-existing drift. Both filed on docs/tasks/backend-ibkr-primary-data-provider-followups.json.
decisions.rationale: This task's own checklist item 1 and the provider-selection work it enables are already a substantial, self-contained change; per this task's explicit 'fine to scope conservatively... push one lower-priority piece to a followups task' guidance, neither of these two findings blocks the core IBKR-primary-OHLCV feature this task implements, and both are more cleanly fixed as their own dedicated, reviewable changes than folded into this PR's diff. (1) is a real, live-confirmed limitation worth tracking since it affects the single most common example ticker in this codebase. (2) is pre-existing drift unrelated to this task's own diff -- bundling a frontend types regeneration that includes several unrelated backend PRs' docstring changes into this task's PR would make this PR's own diff much harder to review and attribute.

decisions.decision: PR #369's needs_work review (3 blocking findings) addressed in this pass: (1) `_resolve_stk_conid` (app/data/ibkr_provider.py) now prefers a candidate whose search-result `description` field names a primary US exchange (new `_US_PRIMARY_EXCHANGES = frozenset({"NASDAQ", "NYSE", "AMEX", "ARCA", "BATS"})`) over degrading to `None` when more than one distinct STK conid matches a bare symbol search, rather than reverting the prior decision above to leave this unfixed. Re-verified the live gateway was still authenticated before doing this research (`get_gateway_status()` returned `available` against `backend/.env`'s configured host) and queried `/iserver/secdef/search` fresh for AAPL, MSFT, GOOGL, TSLA, NVDA, AMZN, IBM, KO, F, GE, SPY, QQQ, CROX, CELH, RUN, PLTR, SNOW, ZS, DDOG, COIN, SAVA: every heavily-tracked US ticker returned exactly one candidate whose top-level `description` was `"NASDAQ"`/`"NYSE"`/`"ARCA"` (the primary US listing) alongside 1-4 further candidates on IBKR's own international feeder-exchange programs (`"TSE"`, `"MEXI"`, `"EBS"`, `"GETTEX"`, `"FWB"`, `"VALUE"`, `"BVME"`, `"ASX"`, `"PURE"`, `"AQSE"`, `"LSEETF"`, `"IBIS"`, `"CDE"`) -- confirming this is the norm for popular US names, not an AAPL-specific edge case, and that `description` (a field on each top-level search-result candidate, NOT nested under `sections`) is a reliable, live-confirmed disambiguation signal. DDOG (only one STK candidate, NASDAQ) confirmed the fix doesn't change behavior for an already-unambiguous ticker. SAVA unexpectedly returned only a single MEXI-listed candidate under a company name unrelated to the historically NASDAQ-listed Cassava Sciences (apparently a ticker-symbol reassignment after a corporate rename) -- noted but not pursued further, since it's an unrelated single-candidate (non-ambiguous) edge case this task's own resolve_conid contract already handles correctly (resolves to whatever the sole candidate is), not a disambiguation problem. (2) tests/integration/test_stocks_analysis_provider_session_race.py's `_racing_providers` fixture now also sets `FINTRADE_IBKR_ENABLED=false` + `get_settings().cache_clear()` (mirroring the 3 tests PR #369 already fixed) -- independently re-confirmed via socket-connect tracing (monkeypatching `socket.socket.connect` to record+reject every outbound call) that this fixed test makes zero outbound connection attempts, and re-ran the same trace across the full 1533-test suite (previously the single file with 3 live connect attempts) to confirm no other test in the suite makes a live network call. (3) docs/architecture/Backend.md §8 (heading, module-table entry, opening paragraphs) rewritten to describe IBKRDataProvider/IBKRPrimaryDataProvider as the app's primary OHLCV source when connected, including a new 'Conid disambiguation for cross-listed tickers' paragraph documenting finding (1)'s fix and research; the `resolve_conid` endpoint bullet and the 'known, accepted limitation' paragraph were also updated to reflect what's now live-confirmed vs. still only documented. Also addressed the one non-blocking finding (`CachedDataProvider(YFinanceProvider(), StooqProvider(), db)` duplicated in app/api/dependencies.py) by factoring it into `_build_yfinance_stooq_provider(db)`, and fixed `get_data_provider_factory`'s stale docstring claim (another already-tracked non-blocking finding) while in the area -- both already marked resolved on docs/tasks/backend-ibkr-primary-data-provider-followups.json rather than left open there.
decisions.rationale: (1): guessing blindly (e.g. assuming USD-denomination or a hardcoded symbol-to-conid table) would have risked a wrong disambiguation signal that happened to work for the handful of tickers tested but broke for others; querying 20 real tickers against the live gateway (rather than just AAPL/MSFT as a minimum) gave confidence `description` is a structural property of every search-result candidate (present even on non-STK/bond rows, just `null` there) rather than a coincidence of a couple of examples. `description`'s sibling field `companyHeader` (e.g. "APPLE INC - NASDAQ") also encodes the exchange, but as a suffix of a free-text string requiring string-splitting rather than an exact-match lookup against a small known set -- `description` alone is simpler and was sufficient for every ticker tested, so `companyHeader` wasn't used. Preferring a primary-exchange match over the full candidate set, rather than e.g. always picking the lowest conid or the first list entry, is robust to whatever order IBKR's own search happens to return results in (observed consistently NASDAQ/NYSE-first in this research, but not relied upon). Still degrading to `None` when the primary-exchange filter itself doesn't leave exactly one candidate (not observed live, but structurally possible -- e.g. a ticker dual-listed on both NASDAQ and NYSE) preserves the original design's core principle (don't silently guess among genuinely ambiguous candidates) rather than trading one kind of silent-wrong-guess risk for another. (2): the fix mirrors the exact pattern already established by the 3 other tests in this same PR rather than inventing a new convention, and the socket-trace re-verification (not just trusting the env-var fix 'should' work) directly addresses the reviewer's own concern that a passing test doesn't by itself prove no live call happened. (3): Backend.md is this project's own designated 'source of truth for how it's built' (CLAUDE.md) -- leaving it describing the reversed decision's predecessor state, after both the code and the module docstring already reflected the reversal, would have left the one audience (a future human or agent reading architecture docs rather than source) most likely to be misled by exactly the stale framing the reviewer flagged.

decisions.decision: Correction to the immediately preceding decisions entry: it describes PR #369's review as having '3 blocking findings', but `review.comments`/`review.notes` on this very task file actually record FOUR blocking findings as of this entry's own timestamp -- a 4th (OHLCV SQLite cache cross-contamination between IBKR-primary and yfinance-primary mode, `OHLCVCacheORM` having no `source`/provider column) was added via a PR comment amendment to the already-posted review, timestamped before that entry's own work began. That 4th finding was NOT addressed by the preceding decisions entry's fixes (1)-(3), an oversight (not a deliberate scope cut) -- it's fixed in this same commit/pass instead of being left for yet another needs_work round: added `OHLCVCacheORM.source` (app/db/models.py, nullable `String`, NOT part of the primary key, migration `b9428ca17553_add_source_to_ohlcv_cache`), set by `CachedDataProvider.__init__` to `type(primary).__name__` (`app/data/cache.py`) and stamped onto every row `_upsert` writes; `_get`'s freshness check now reads via a new `_read_cache_for_current_source` (filtered by `self._source`) instead of the unfiltered `_read_cache` (which stays unfiltered, deliberately, since `_upsert`'s own existing-row lookup still needs to find and overwrite an other-source row in place by its (ticker, date, interval) primary key rather than attempting a duplicate INSERT at an already-occupied key). New `TestCrossSourceContamination` test class (tests/unit/data/test_cache.py, 5 tests) directly reproduces the reviewer's own repro scenario in both directions plus the legacy-NULL-source and same-source-still-hits cases.
decisions.rationale: Fixing this now (rather than filing it as a 5th -followups item and shipping another needs_work round) follows the same reasoning CLAUDE.md's decision-memory section gives for judgment calls a worker can resolve itself: this is squarely inside this task's own explicit 'use IBKR exclusively' requirement (the review's own wording -- 'this directly contradicts this task's own explicit requirement... and the PR's own commit message'), not a tangential nit, and the fix itself (a nullable, non-PK column plus a source-matching filter on the read path only) is small and self-contained relative to re-running a whole review/fix cycle for one finding alone. Chose `type(primary).__name__` over e.g. a caller-supplied string constant specifically so no existing call site (`app.api.dependencies`, nor any of the dozens of direct `CachedDataProvider(primary, fallback, db)` constructions across the test suite) needed to change at all -- the tag falls out of the object graph `app.api.dependencies` already builds differently for IBKR-primary vs. yfinance-primary mode, rather than requiring a new parameter threaded through every caller. Kept `source` nullable with no backfill (rather than a NOT NULL column with a migration-time backfill pass) since a pre-existing row simply reads as a miss for whichever source becomes active post-migration -- a one-time, harmless extra refetch per already-cached ticker/interval, not a correctness problem worth a backfill migration's added complexity. Deliberately did NOT make `_read_cache` (the `_upsert`-dedup lookup) source-filtered too -- tried this first and it reproduces exactly the `IntegrityError`-on-every-mode-switch failure mode `_upsert`'s own existing `except (IntegrityError, OperationalError)` block is documented as being for a *different*, genuinely-concurrent race, not a deterministic every-single-switch failure; keeping `_read_cache` source-agnostic for `_upsert`'s own existing-row lookup avoids silently relying on that except block to paper over a different, actually-expected code path. Did not touch `ExtendedDataCacheORM`: extended data is never routed to IBKR at all (this task's own earlier decisions entry -- a permanent carve-out to the cached yfinance/Stooq chain regardless of IBKR connectivity), so there is no second source to cross-contaminate against for that cache table.

questions.context: Re-ran the exact same live-gateway checks as the original questions entry before doing any implementation work, per this task's resumption instructions. `IBKRProvider(base_url='https://ibkr.home.arpa/v1/api').get_gateway_status()` now returns `GatewayStatus(state='gateway_unreachable', detail='IBKR gateway returned HTTP 401 from /iserver/auth/status')` -- a different symptom than the original blocker's `not_authenticated`/400 'no bridge' response, but still not usable. Direct httpx calls confirm this isn't a transient blip: GET /iserver/auth/status, /iserver/accounts, /iserver/marketdata/history, and /iserver/secdef/search all return a bare HTTP 401 with an empty body (not the 'no bridge' JSON seen before), and a fresh `x-sess-uuid` cookie is minted on every single request even when the client's cookie jar already holds one from a prior response in the same session, i.e. no session is being recognized at all. Crucially, `GET /` (no path) redirects (302) to `/sso/Login?forwardTo=22&RL=1&ip2loc=US`, which serves a genuine IBKR login HTML page (bootstrap/jquery CP Gateway login UI, confirmed by fetching and reading the page body) -- this is the standard CP Gateway behavior for an unauthenticated session, not a proxy/network artifact (GET /v1/portal correctly 302s to https://api.ibkr.com/v1/portal, and the TLS cert is a blank self-signed one valid 2026-2036, both consistent with talking to a genuine self-hosted clientportal.gw instance via this reverse-proxied host, not a misconfigured or unrelated service -- the server-timing headers that initially looked Akamai-branded are plausibly passed through from IBKR's own backend, which the gateway proxies to). In short: whatever host this task's live-gateway research must run against is still presenting its own login page rather than an authenticated session, despite the user's confirmation -- possibly because the interactive login was completed against a different gateway instance/URL (e.g. a direct https://localhost:5000 session on the user's own machine, distinct from whatever process backs https://ibkr.home.arpa from this devcontainer's network path) than the one FINTRADE_IBKR_BASE_URL in backend/.env actually points this app at, or because the session already expired again since confirming. No implementation work was done in this pass -- per this task's own checklist item 1, the live-gateway research (history depth ceiling, extended-data equivalents) genuinely cannot be confirmed without a working authenticated session reachable at the configured base URL, and guessing would violate the task's own explicit instruction not to assume.

Non-blocking (found via a backgrounded code-review pass on this round's fix commits, not previously flagged): `CachedDataProvider._read_cache_for_current_source`'s docstring overstates the cache-cross-contamination fix -- it claims a mode switch overwrites the other chain's rows in place 'rather than leaving a second, duplicate set of rows behind', but that only holds for dates within the new source's own fetched range. IBKR's daily history is confirmed live to be ~999 bars (~4 calendar years) -- far shallower than yfinance's full history -- so a ticker with years of pre-existing yfinance rows that switches to IBKR-primary will have `_upsert` overwrite only the overlapping ~4-year window; older yfinance-tagged rows outside it are never revisited and sit in the table indefinitely (harmless -- still correctly filtered out as a miss -- but the docstring's claim is inaccurate and the table silently grows over repeated mode switches).
